kept.spine: What the town keeps for its own safety answers what it faces, and a further demand could be met only by leaving something else uncovered.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls with NO force
kept.spine: The walls are kept up and no soldiers of the town's own stand on them.
faces: {elders} {v:take} the walls for their own boundary before anything else, and where the line runs is the older argument.
A night patrolman says the walk along the wall falls to the watch, and the watch has the streets to keep as well.
A clerk of the court says what is disputed about the walls is always who owes the work and never who would hold them.
The people of the town have seen the walls kept and no one standing on them, and take it that no one is coming.

kept.poolKey: Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)
kept.spine: A complaint brought here is heard in the courthouse, and the town has a cell for whoever it names.
faces: One of the aldermen says the court takes matters in their order, and a man who complains of waiting is waiting on the matter before his.
A drover says a man held here waits until somebody says whose business he is.
A bailiff says a stranger's complaint is heard in its turn and that most strangers are gone before the turn comes.
A woman at the long table says a man is called in for who he knows and let out for what he can pay.
The watch says a man taken up at night is theirs as far as the cell door and no further.
A soldier reckons a stranger stopped at the gate is the garrison's until his business is asked. After that he is the watch's.
A guild factor says the trades pay twice for a matter at the court, in the man who waits and in the work waiting with him.
The stallholders say a cheated stranger is told where to bring the matter, and a cheated stallholder is told the same after the stranger has gone.
The men who hold the way in say a stranger with a complaint against him waits at the gate until somebody from the court comes for him.

kept.poolKey: Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only
kept.spine: The town keeps a grain store against a bad harvest and no house for the sick, so the sick are tended out of the parish.
faces: A local priest says a stranger asks for the sick house and is sent to whoever does the nursing.
The traders at the fair say the town buys their grain to fill its store and sells them nothing back out of it.
The inn servants say a guest who takes sick is nursed at the inn and nobody comes for him.
One of the watch says strangers ask where the grain is kept and no stranger asks where the sick are taken.
A master of one of the crafts says the trades filled the store and cannot open it.
A woman who brought a matter to the court says grain is argued over there and the nursing of the sick never is.

kept.spine: The safety of the streets at Spitzplatz sits where either side could take it, and a thinner watch or a bolder gang would be enough to tip it.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: What the town says about its own safety is what it says to a newcomer, and what it says to somebody who has stayed is another account.
Casual violence is rare in the streets here, and what keeps it rare is not the watch.
The walls here are whole, and every way in is a way the town chose to leave open.
People walk the town at night, and the town counts that for more than it counts the walls.
The charter hall takes the sort of trouble the watch is the wrong answer to, and it is not short of work.
The town's defences include wards and a way of knowing when something unseen has come in, and both are kept at the alchemist's shop.
The town walls at Spitzplatz are sound, and the purse that keeps them falls short of the keeping.

kept.poolKey: Logistics & Supply: Granary with road supply
kept.spine: What the town does not grow comes in by road, and the grain store is what stands between a blocked road and an empty table.
